examples.name: Sanchay
examples.subtitle: Personal finance · local-first
examples.summary: A React + TypeScript personal-finance dashboard hosted in an Android WebView. Ledger data lives in browser local storage; there is no deployed server backend.

adapter.display_name: Financial reports: original vs single-pass aggregation
adapter.change_summary: The Reports page currently walks the currency-scoped ledger three times: once for totals, once for category spending and once for payees. The candidate produces the same three results in one shared traversal.
adapter.mechanism: One pass accumulates minor-unit totals, category spending and payee amounts. The existing minor-unit money helpers and the existing ordering/filtering rules are retained.
correctness_rules: Totals, category breakdown and payee breakdown must match the original byte-for-byte after JSON canonicalisation.
Refunds reduce spending and payee totals exactly as the original does; they never become income.
Transfers are excluded from spending and payees; only completed goal debits count as saved.
Pending, failed and flagged transactions never contribute to a completed report.
Currencies are never combined; each report is scoped to one currency before aggregation.
JPY (zero minor digits) and two-decimal currencies keep their existing precision.
Results are deterministic and the original ledger array is not mutated.
adapter.scope_note: This evaluates a client-side report-calculation strategy. It does not evaluate API replicas, a server queue, PostgreSQL, or cloud failover, because Sanchay has no deployed server backend.

examples.name: Flask + Redis sample
examples.subtitle: Genuine public backend · awesome-compose
examples.summary: Docker’s public Flask + Redis Compose sample. A hit counter stored in Redis is served by a Flask app. DARWIN does not run the repository Compose file; it deploys a reviewed isolated stack (gunicorn, nginx, official Redis) from app.py and requirements.txt only.

adapter.change_summary: Baseline is one Flask replica with one gunicorn worker. Candidates add a second replica behind nginx, or a second worker on the original replica. Redis stays shared.
adapter.mechanism: DARWIN copies flask-redis/app.py into a DARWIN-owned image, generates nginx + Compose, drives seeded HTTP GET /, checks that the Redis counter increases, and optionally restarts one replica to measure recovery.
correctness_rules: GET / returns the reviewed Flask counter sentence.
The viewed-count integer strictly increases through the gateway (shared Redis).
A restarted web replica becomes healthy again on loopback.
adapter.scope_note: This evaluates deployable process topology for one public sample. It does not convert Flask to another framework, invent a SQL database, or run the repository Dockerfile.

policy.inspection: Public HTTPS GitHub repositories may be inspected after explicit consent.
policy.execution: Only catalogued repositories at the pinned commit may run an audited adapter.
policy.recorded_label: Saved results are always labelled recorded, never live.
policy.backend_isolation: Linux Docker engine required. Repository Compose files are never executed.

screening.label: SIMULATED
screening.scope_note: Models deployment-level architecture variants from inspected source. No repository code is executed and no runtime is measured.
